comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C64, C71 regarding the identification of nine type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing based on experimental observations in Figures 3-4 with appropriate molecular markers.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C4, C33, C34, C36, C37 regarding lineage size differences between Tribolium and Drosophila. Both evaluations accept the quantitative data in Tables 1-2 and Figure 9. Peer review also includes C35 (mitotic activity) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Complete agreement on claims C31, C32 regarding central complex contribution. Both evaluations accept the co-staining experiments with skh reporter line showing lineage contribution to central complex structures.

Agreement on claims C18, C19, C62 regarding the fez-mm-eGFP enhancer trap line. Both evaluations acknowledge successful generation and utility of this tool. Peer review also includes C20, C21, C63 which OpenEval addresses in R9 and R11.

Agreement on molecular characterization claims C24-C30, C76-C78, C118. Both evaluations accept the expression patterns of conserved markers. However, peer review notes a caveat about lack of unequivocal neuroblast markers in Tribolium. OpenEval R3 covers 11 claims while peer R4 covers 19 claims including additional markers (C22, C23, C58-C60, C72, C73, C119).

Strong agreement on claims C44, C79, C80, C84, C88 regarding the hypothesis linking type II neuroblast characteristics to embryonic central complex development. Both evaluations recognize this as a hypothesis requiring further validation. Peer review explicitly states the manuscript 'does not establish a direct link' and notes this as a weakness. Both acknowledge C85 (need for confirmation).

Agreement on Tc-six4 expression claims C7, C39-C42. Both evaluations accept the RNA in situ hybridization data showing spatial and temporal patterns. Peer R5 also includes C5, C6, C38, C43, C102 regarding Tc-otd and Tc-six3 expression, which OpenEval addresses separately in R5 and R6.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C38 regarding absence of Tc-otd expression in type II neuroblasts. Both evaluations accept the negative result from RNA in situ hybridization. Peer R5 covers broader set including C6, C7, C39-C43, C102 regarding multiple transcription factors.

Partial overlap on claims C6, C43, C102 regarding Tc-six3 expression in anterior lineages. Both evaluations accept the spatial restriction data. Peer R5 covers broader transcription factor analysis including Tc-otd and Tc-six4.

Agreement on claims C67, C68, C69, C70 regarding spatial organization and grouping of neuroblasts. Both evaluations accept these descriptive findings about cluster arrangements. OpenEval R17 also includes C66 which provides literature context.

Partial overlap on claims C111, C112 regarding absence of Tc-otd and Tc-six3 in specific lineages and implications for protocerebral models. Both evaluations accept these findings. Peer R9 covers broader set C106-C112 regarding central complex tract organization and six3 function.

Partial overlap on claims C20, C21 regarding developmental progression of Tc-pnt-expressing clusters. Both evaluations accept the systematic imaging data. OpenEval R9 also includes C67 about cluster numbers.

Agreement on claims C22, C23 regarding quantitative cell size measurements confirming neuroblast identity. Both evaluations accept the statistical analysis showing significant differences in cell and nuclear diameter.

Partial overlap on claim C35 regarding mitotic activity measured by PH3 staining. Both evaluations accept this as a reasonable estimate of proliferative activity, though OpenEval notes the limitation that PH3 marks only specific mitotic phases.

Agreement on claims C72, C73 regarding Tc-pnt and Tc-fez/erm co-expression in immature INPs and functional conservation. Both evaluations accept the overlap data and inference of conserved function based on Drosophila comparisons.

Agreement on claim C119 regarding conservation of molecular signatures between Tribolium and Drosophila. Both evaluations accept the comprehensive molecular characterization. OpenEval R18 also includes C120 about spatial patterning candidates.

Disagreement on claims C103-C106 regarding central complex tract organization. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting that direct lineage tracing in Tribolium is needed to confirm Tc-six3-positive lineages produce specific tracts. Peer review accepts these claims as SUPPORTED based on expression patterns and cross-species comparisons.

Potential disagreement on claims C65, C98, C100, C101 regarding evolutionary mechanisms and Tc-six4 function. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting these are speculative and require functional experiments. Peer review appears to accept the broader transcription factor characterization as SUPPORTED without explicitly addressing the functional speculation.

Both address claim C85 acknowledging need for further confirmation of the central complex hypothesis. OpenEval rates this acknowledgment as SUPPORTED (appropriate scientific practice), while peer review rates the broader hypothesis (C44, C79-C84, C88) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct evidence.

OpenEval R19 covers 41 claims (C10-C11, C45-C61, C74-C75, C82-C83, C86-C97, C107-C110, C113-C117) that are appropriately cited literature providing context. These background claims are not explicitly evaluated as separate results in peer review, though some appear embedded in other peer results (e.g., C82-C83 in R7, C107-C110 in R9).

OpenEval R20 covers background claims C8-C9, C12-C17 about established knowledge and the gap this study addresses. These contextual claims are not explicitly evaluated as separate results in peer review.
